name: Netanya cliff protection: detached breakwaters, submerged reefs and nourishment
year_built: Phase 1 (6 breakwaters, north): construction started April 2021, preliminary drilling reportedly 2019, completed ~September 2023. Phase 2 (6 breakwaters, south): groundbreaking 6 Aug 2024, completed/handed over 3-4 June 2026
closed: not applicable - project completed and operating; land-side (terrestrial) cliff protection track remains separately underfunded nationally
type: 12 detached rubble-mound rock breakwaters (mix of emergent and submerged), quarried core + armor stone, plus pumped-sand beach nourishment
purpose: Stop erosion/collapse of Netanya's ~40 m kurkar coastal cliffs threatening the promenade, buildings and public safety; widen public beach as a byproduct

dimensions.sand_phase2_m3: 250000 (most sources) vs 480000 (one Netanya-local outlet at approval stage) - disagreement not resolved

designer: Not named in accessible sources; early marine-model plans credited to then-city-engineer Paul Weitel; ASCE/ResearchGate engineering paper on the design was blocked (HTTP 403)
contractor: Ocean Ltd (אושן התחדשות עירונית) per its own project portfolio, execution window 2020-2023; unconfirmed whether same contractor executed phase 2 (2024-2026)

cost.note: figures disagree across project stages/outlets; the ~360M NIS figure in the original seed note is very likely the countrywide (not Netanya-only) maritime cliff-protection budget cited by the Environment Minister at a Jan 2025 Knesset hearing, of which 330M NIS had already been spent nationally

financed_by: Israeli government (Ministry of Environmental Protection budget, one account traces it to Israel Land Authority revenue) via the state-owned Government Company for Protection of Mediterranean Sea Cliffs; separately Netanya municipality spent its own ~80M NIS on parallel land-side works
outcome_one_liner: 12 rubble-mound breakwaters (~1,400 m total) plus ~450,000+ m3 of pumped sand were built 2021-2026 (~190M NIS, ~6 years, about double the originally projected ~3-year timeline) along 3.5 km of Netanya's kurkar cliff; the company's CEO credited the completed northern phase with halting collapses there as of April 2023, while national State Comptroller and Knesset reviews (2024-2025) found most of Israel's cliff coast, including Netanya's own land-side track, still under-protected due to a split Environmental Protection vs Interior ministry funding structure; public reaction was mixed - a mid-2026 Haaretz feature likened the finished breakwaters to islands blocking the horizon 'like Dubai' even while calling the widened beach itself pleasant; no source found measuring the project's effect on the pre-existing Sironit/Kontiki surf break, and the origin (natural/artificial/wreck) of Poleg Beach's two offshore submerged reefs flagged in Lior's notes remains unresolved.
